skill.name: bevy-ecs-expert

skill.summary: Guide Bevy ECS design with practical Rust examples for game logic and performance.

static_findings.snippet: Use simple structs for data. Derive `Component` and `Reflect`.
Use `Resource` for global data (score, game state).
Add systems to the `App` builder, defining execution order if needed.
Use `With` and `Without` to filter entities efficiently.
- ✅ **Do:** Use `Query` filters (`With`, `Without`, `Changed`) to reduce iteration count.
- ✅ **Do:** Prefer `Res` over `ResMut` when read-only access is sufficient to allow parallel executi
- ✅ **Do:** Use `Bundle` to spawn complex entities atomically.
- ❌ **Don't:** Use `RefCell` or interior mutability inside components; let the ECS handle borrowing.

content.value_statement: Bevy ECS can be hard to structure when systems, resources, and queries grow together. This skill gives concise Rust guidance for data-oriented game logic in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to define Bevy components and bundles for game entities.
Shows how to write systems that query and mutate ECS data safely.
Guides use of resources for global game state and shared data.
Demonstrates scheduling systems with ordering and parallel execution concerns.
Provides query filter guidance using With, Without, and Changed patterns.
Helps refactor object-oriented game logic into data-oriented ECS design.
limitations: It is a compact guide, not a complete Bevy manual.
Examples are illustrative and may need updates for specific Bevy versions.
It does not run, compile, or test Rust projects by itself.
It focuses on ECS architecture, not rendering, networking, or asset pipelines.

use_cases.title: Design a Bevy Player Entity
use_cases.description: Plan components, bundles, and setup systems for a player entity with movement data.

use_cases.title: Refactor Game Logic
use_cases.description: Convert object-oriented update logic into Bevy systems, resources, and query filters.

use_cases.title: Improve ECS Performance
use_cases.description: Review query filters and resource access patterns to reduce work and allow parallel scheduling.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Bevy ECS Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how Bevy components, systems, queries, resources, and bundles work together. Use a small game example without raw code.

prompt_templates.title: Design My Entity Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for a new gameplay feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design Bevy ECS components, bundles, and resources for this feature: [describe feature]. Explain why each piece belongs there.

prompt_templates.title: Review My System Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of existing Bevy logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Bevy ECS system structure for borrow conflicts, query efficiency, and resource usage. Suggest clearer system boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Parallel Scheduling
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Bevy ECS design for parallel scheduling opportunities. Identify unnecessary mutable access, ordering constraints, and query filters to improve.

output_examples.input: I need enemies that chase the player and stop when defeated.
output_examples.output: Suggested design: separate movement, enemy state, target selection, and defeat marker data. Use filters to skip defeated enemies and keep movement independent.

output_examples.input: My score system blocks other systems from running in parallel.
output_examples.output: Expected guidance: read shared state immutably when possible, isolate score updates, and order only the systems with real data conflicts.

output_examples.input: I want to spawn a complex player entity cleanly.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: group related components in a bundle and keep setup logic focused on entity creation and asset references.

best_practices: Keep components as data and place behavior in systems.
Use query filters to reduce unnecessary iteration.
Prefer immutable resource access when a system only reads shared state.
anti_patterns: Do not hide gameplay logic inside component data types.
Do not use mutable resources when read-only access is enough.
Do not force system ordering unless a real data dependency exists.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design Bevy ECS game logic with components, systems, queries, resources, bundles, and schedules.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it compile my Rust project?
faq.answer: No. It provides design and review guidance, but it does not run Rust builds by itself.

faq.question: Is this only for game developers?
faq.answer: It is mainly for Bevy game developers, but ECS design lessons can help other data-oriented Rust projects.

faq.question: Can it help with performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers query filters, resource access, and scheduling choices that affect Bevy ECS performance.

faq.question: Does it cover all Bevy systems?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on ECS architecture and does not fully cover rendering, assets, networking, or UI.
